title.narrative: DRA - Yemen Joint Response 2024-2026

description.narrative: The overall objective of the YJR (24-26) is to provide multifaceted, life-saving humanitarian support to those in need, prioritizing the most vulnerable. ZOA continues to work with SDF. This 36-months response is divided over DFA- and IRG-areas. In Hajjah Governorate, ZOA will implement WASH and GCT. In Al Dhale'e Governorate, ZOA will implement GCT. SDF will implement GCT in Hajjah and Protection services in Al Dhale'e. Key targeted groups include 1) women, 2) people living with a disability, 3) communities with high SAM & MAM rates, 4) youth, 5) children and 6) GBV-survivors.

title.narrative: Adequate WASH services and practices

description.narrative: 72010 - Adequate WASH services and practices

title.narrative: WSH-IO1 - % of target population with adequate WASH services and hygiene practices

description.narrative: The target population considering that their basic WASH needs are met and the target population with adequate hygiene practices (according to SPHERE standards on appropriate use and regular maintenance of facilities and hand washing) will be measured after the intervention.

comment.narrative: Baseline results have shown that only 7% were with adequate access to WASH service and hygiene practices. Updated figures will be reported at the endline assessment.
SA is approved. Delay from authorities due to the selection of appropriate water resources. More progress is expected within the next reporting period.

title.narrative: Using cash

description.narrative: 72040 - Using cash

title.narrative: CSH-IO1 - % of households who report being able to meet the basic needs of their households (all/most/some/none), according to their priorities.

description.narrative: 60% of households report being able to meet all or most of the basic needs of their households according to their priorities.

comment.narrative: (88.8%) reported being able to meet only some of their basic needs, indicating ongoing struggles to fully address essential requirements. Only 9% of households met half of their needs, while 0.98% could meet most of their priorities, and another 0.98% were unable to meet any basic needs. This finding came from a PDM conducted by SDF after the distribution of cash to the groups.
18% of HH report being able to meet all or most of their HHs basic needs. The finding is the average gathered from PDM results conducted by both ZOA and SDF throughout the year till end of September

title.narrative: Protection

description.narrative: 72050 - Protection

title.narrative: PRO-IO1 - "% of targeted persons reporting an increased sense of safety and well-being after engaging in the protection activities under this project "

description.narrative: After the intervention, we anticipate that 95% of targeted individuals will report an increased sense of safety and well-being after engaging in the protection activities. The measurement will be done by assessing selected beneficiaries by the CBPNs and conducting post-distribution monitoring (PDM) on the provision of protection cash assistance, legal cash assistance, GBV cash assistance, and livelihood and skills-building activities. The M&E team will develop an M&E tool to be used in order to collect data.

comment.narrative: SA is approved; however, activities will only start next year by the local partner.
Updates on this indicator was not reporting in this reporting period and is expected to be reported at the endline evaluation.

description.narrative: ZOA and SDF plan to support 92 groups. It is estimated that 20 HHs will directly benefit per group cash transfer * average HH size of 7 = 12880 people. ZOA= 50 groups and SDF 42 groups.

comment.narrative: 5474 individuals have benefited from 21 GCTs being implemented by ZOA and 2 by the local partner SDF. Additionally, a total of 3787 individuals have benefited from the one-off round of cash assistance as part of the crisis modifier budget.
